claim: Kelly criterion: maximize expected log growth
head: A New Interpretation of Information Rate reproduced with permission of AT&T By J. L. Kelly, jr. (Manuscript received March 21, 1956) If the input symbols to a communication channel represent the outcomes of a chance event on which bets are available at odds consistent with their probabilities (i.e., \fair" odds), a gambler can use the knowledge given him by the received symbols to cause his money to grow exponentially. The maximum exponential rate of growth of the gambler’s capital is equal to the rate of transmission of information over the channel. This result is generalized to include the case of arbitrary odds. Thus we ﬂnd a situation in which the transmission rate is signiﬂcant even though no coding is contemplated. Previously this quantity was given signiﬂcance only by a theorem of Shannon’s which asserted that, with suitable encoding, binary digits could be transmitted over the channel at this rate with an arbitrarily small probability of error. introduction Shannon deﬂnes the rate of transmission over a noisy communication channel in terms of various probabilities. 1 This deﬂnition is given signiﬂcance by a theorem which asserts that binary digits may be encoded and transmitted over the channel at this rate with arbitrarily small probability of error. Many workers in the ﬂeld of communication theory have felt a desire to attach signiﬂcance to the rate of transmission in cases where no coding was contemplated.
